Commit:  541b3a78026420a3e369c4c9281c396b5e531113 (2024-11-13)
Copied on 2026-11-14. Compiled only through sv2curve.c, which sets its options.

ONE LOCAL CHANGE (2026-11-15), asm_avr.inc only: "memory" added to the clobber
list of all 14 inline-assembly statements. Without it GCC 16 assumes the
assembly never reads or writes the arrays it is handed pointers to, warns that
they "may be used uninitialized", and miscompiles the callers: the first curve
operation crashed and reset the ATmega. Every other file is unmodified.

SECOND LOCAL CHANGE (2026-11-15), asm_avr.inc only: uECC_vli_add and
uECC_vli_sub (the optimization-level-2 versions) store through register Z, but
the instruction that loads Z with the result pointer sits in a jump table that
is only compiled when more than one curve size is enabled. With secp256k1 alone
Z was never loaded, so every add/subtract wrote 32 bytes to a stray address
(seen in the disassembly; it crashed the ATmega in the first field operation).
Fix: "movw r30, %A[result]" added in the single-size case of both functions.

THIRD LOCAL CHANGE (2026-11-16), uECC.c only: three lines at the top of the
main loop of EccPoint_mult call the macro uECC_YIELD() if the including file
defines it. sv2curve.c uses it so the miner can answer its serial console
during the multi-second multiplications. Without the macro the library is
unchanged.
